extracted.intended_audience: practitioners before the USPTO (patent/trademark attorneys), disciplinary counsel, and attorneys facing reciprocal discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Procedure and standards for imposing reciprocal discipline by the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 when an attorney has been disciplined by a state authority, including notice requirements, available defenses, and possible sanctions (e.g., public reprimand).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Action taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 to impose discipline in the USPTO based on state disciplinary action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 as the statutory and regulatory basis for imposing reciprocal discipline; disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the OED FOIA Reading Room (http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for reciprocal discipline (predicate state discipline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline may be imposed where the discipline by a state is predicated on ethical misconduct in that jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO reprimanded Respondent for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), predicated upon receiving a reprimand on ethical grounds by a duly constituted authority of a state; the Order incorporated the findings of the state's Disciplinary Review Board (Docket No. DRB 17-191).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond (37 C.F.R. § 11.24 process)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must send a 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' notifying the respondent of the Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline and providing an opportunity to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case the Notice and Order was sent by certified mail (receipt no. provided) and provided the Respondent 40 days to file a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more of the reasons in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). Delivery date and receipt are relevant procedural facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response to the Notice and Order, the USPTO may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and proceed to impose reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Here, Respondent did not file a response to the Notice and Order; the OED Director determined there was no genuine issue of material fact and that a public reprimand was the appropriate discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Available defenses under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may oppose imposition of reciprocal discipline by asserting one or more reasons set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order explicitly provided the opportunity to oppose based on the statutory/regulatory grounds in § 11.24(d)(1) (the Order references those available defenses even though it does not list them in full).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content of imposed discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may impose discipline identical to that imposed by the state, such as a public reprimand with terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this proceeding the USPTO imposed a public reprimand and directed publication of a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the reprimand and the state order; discipline may mirror state-imposed terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirement (Official Gazette notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the public reprimand and the reasons for the discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample Notice includes the respondent's name and location, authorization to practice areas, the fact that the reprimand is reciprocal and predicated on a state reprimand, and summarizes the state Court's Order and required terms (e.g., submission of reconciliations, reimbursement of costs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to other authorities (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice of the public discipline and the reasons to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is admitted, and to the public under 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order directs the OED Director to give notice pursuant to § 11.59 to the relevant state disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-imposed remedial terms that may be incorporated
rubrics_metrics.description: State courts may impose remedial conditions (e.g., account monitoring, record submissions, reimbursement of costs) that the USPTO may describe or incorporate in its notice of discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Supreme Court of New Jersey ordered Respondent to 'submit to the Office of Attorney Ethics, on a quarterly basis, monthly reconciliations of his attorney accounts for two years and until further Order of the Court' and to 'reimburse the Disciplinary Oversight Committee for appropriate administrative costs and actual expenses incurred in the prosecution of this matter' — these terms are summarized in the Official Gazette notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific ethical violations relied upon
rubrics_metrics.description: The disciplinary action was predicated on violations of New Jersey Rule of Professional Conduct (RPC) 1.15(a) and RPC 1.15(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RPC 1.15(a): failure to safeguard client funds and negligent misappropriation of client funds; RPC 1.15(d): failure to comply with record keeping requirements (rule 1:21-6). The Order explains factual bases: mismanaged client trust account, insufficient funds upon issuing a check to a client, and failure to keep proper accounting records resulting in failure to safeguard other clients' funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipulation of discipline by consent
rubrics_metrics.description: A stipulation of discipline by consent between the Office of Attorney Ethics and the respondent may form the factual and legal basis for the state discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order notes that the Office of Attorney Ethics and Respondent signed a stipulation of discipline by consent on May 15, 2017, in which it was agreed Respondent violated the cited RPC provisions; such stipulations are relevant evidence in the reciprocal proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of disciplinary decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions are to be made available for public review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs readers to the OED FOIA Reading Room URL for public review of disciplinary decisions; publication and notification requirements ensure public access to the discipline information.
